verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED - whitespace-only formatting difference, no content discrepancy. Both descriptions of the two sources are factually accurate, but the difference is nothing more than leading indentation.

(1) PDF verified at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v401/spec_p401.png, printed page 371). Rule 7)'s six em-dash items sit at roughly one extra indent level relative to the rule's own text; rule 10)'s a)/b)/c) items and the trailing 'where length ...' line sit at the SAME left margin as rule 10)'s wrapped text (i.e. about three character positions right of the '10)' marker, not a deeper level). So the PDF indentation the claim invokes is a shallow ~3-space hang, not a structurally distinct block.

(2) Markdown verified directly in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, lines 17230-17251 (not just the extracted slice). Every character of the text is present, complete, correctly spelled, in the correct reading order, and with every marker intact: the six bullets carry U+2014 EM DASH (codepoint checked: 0x2014), and the a)/b)/c) markers and terminal punctuation ('PICTURE X(length)',  / 'PICTURE 1(length)', or / 'PICTURE N(length)'. ) are all preserved. Nothing is missing, reordered, merged, or reworded. Nothing is 'misplaced' - the kind label is itself wrong, since no content appears anywhere other than where the PDF puts it in reading order. The only delta is 0 leading spaces instead of 3.

(3) The meaning is carried by the prose and the markers, not by the indentation. Rule 7) ends '... shall include at least one of the following:' and rule 8) follows the bullets as a numbered rule; rule 10) ends '... is implied as follows:' and the a)/b)/c) items plus a lowercase, unnumbered 'where length is ...' continuation follow it, with the 13.17.4 heading next. No reader or downstream consumer can mistake an em-dash bullet or a lowercase 'where' clause for a numbered syntax rule, and there is no competing parent rule they could attach to.

(4) The claim's central premise - that page 401 'contradicts the convention' - is false: this transcription has no such convention. Document-wide counts: 572 lettered sub-items flush at column 0 vs 794 indented; 571 em-dash bullet lines flush vs 110 indented. Flush-left is in fact the MAJORITY treatment for em-dash bullets. The very same PICTURE-implication list appears a third time at lines 16763-16769 (page 390, data description rule 14) and there it is indented - so the transcription is mixed for this identical content in three places. That is a pre-existing, document-wide stylistic inconsistency in the transcription pipeline, not a page-401 content defect, and no consumer can rely on indentation as structure anywhere in this file.

Under the rejection criteria this is squarely 'formatting only' and 'does not change meaning'. Filing it as a page-401 discrepancy would also be misleading, since fixing page 401 alone would leave ~570 sibling occurrences untouched.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-401 content discrepancy. The text of rule 7)'s six em-dash items and rule 10)'s a)/b)/c) items plus the 'where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals.' qualifier is transcribed completely and in correct order, with the U+2014 em dashes and lettered markers intact; only the PDF's ~3-space sub-list hang indent is absent. If anything is worth tracking it is a global transcription-style issue, not this page: the pipeline emits sub-list indentation inconsistently across the whole document (572 flush vs 794 indented lettered sub-items; 571 flush vs 110 indented em-dash bullets), including for this identical PICTURE-implication list, which is indented at lines 16765-16769 (page 390 rule 14) and 16947-16953 (page 395 rule 9) but flush at 17245-17251 (page 401 rule 10). Any normalization should be a single document-wide pass, not a per-page fix.
